claim_tested: The design document's Check 5 ('defined behavior under population drift') is fully defined -- including at the boundary where a candidate's future_holdout population vanishes entirely, not merely the smooth 30% shrinkage its own Case E tested.
finding: Case F1 falsifies the design document's Check 5 claim of fully 'defined behavior under population drift': when a candidate's future_holdout exposure is zero (a plausible, not contrived, outcome given discover_candidates selects candidates using only development-split eligibility), the design's own proposed computation -- literally as specified in Sec 1 and implemented in its own diagnostic script's `_calibration_check` -- raises an uncaught AssertionError rather than returning any verdict at all. This is a real gap relative to G10's own existing temporal-stability gate (apply.py lines ~741-757), which already handles an absent future_holdout split defensively (same_sign=False, retention=0.0, gate fails cleanly) precisely because this scenario is a known, expected case for that gate's own inputs -- the same inputs this design proposes to reuse. Cases F2/F3 (population explodes 40x; shrinks to n=5) remain correctly computable and resolve sensibly, confirming the defect is specific to the unguarded zero-population boundary, not the population-drift design generally.
